\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{علت} ('ellat)}{علت ('ellat)}]{\fa{علت} ('ellat) — a cause, a reason}

\label{lesson:FA-C369-ellat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a conclusion, then the Persian for to mention.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{علت}}
\textbf{\fa{علت}} (\emph{'ellat}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cause, a reason\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{علت} \fa{بیماری} \fa{او} \fa{هنوز} \fa{معلوم} \fa{نیست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{'ellat-e bimâri-ye u hanuz ma'lum nist.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cause of his illness is still not known.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{'elal}, an Arabic broken plural. \emph{Be 'ellat-e} — because of.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{علت}} comes from Arabic \emph{'illa} (EtymDB), a word for both a cause and an illness; in Persian it means the cause or reason for something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'ellat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'ellat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'ellat}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a conclusion, then the Persian for to mention, then say \emph{'ellat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عامل} ('âmel)}{عامل ('âmel)}]{\fa{عامل} ('âmel) — a factor; an agent}

\label{lesson:FA-C369-amel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to mention, then the Persian for a cause.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عامل}}
\textbf{\fa{عامل}} (\emph{'âmel}) — \textquotedblleft{}a factor; an agent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پول} \fa{تنها} \fa{عامل} \fa{خوشبختی} \fa{نیست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pul tanhâ 'âmel-e khoshbakhti nist.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Money is not the only factor in happiness.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{'avâmel}, an Arabic broken plural. Also the person who does a deed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{عامل}} comes from Arabic \emph{'āmil} \textquotedblleft{}worker, doer\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): a factor is whatever does the work behind an effect.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'âmel}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to mention, then the Persian for a cause, then say \emph{'âmel} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باعث} \fa{شدن} (bâ'es shodan)}{باعث شدن (bâ'es shodan)}]{\fa{باعث} \fa{شدن} (bâ'es shodan) — to cause}

\label{lesson:FA-C369-baes-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a cause, then the Persian for a factor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باعث} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{باعث} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{bâ'es shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to cause\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{باران} \fa{باعث} \fa{شد} \fa{که} \fa{دیر} \fa{برسیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bârân bâ'es shod ke dir berasim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The rain made us arrive late.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bâ'es} \textquotedblleft{}cause\textquotedblright{} + \emph{shodan} (stem \emph{shav-}). With a noun: \emph{bâ'es-e chizi shodan}; with a clause: \emph{bâ'es shod ke} + subjunctive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{باعث}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{bā'ith} \textquotedblleft{}that which sends or prompts\textquotedblright{}; with the inherited Persian verb \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} it means to be the cause of something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâ'es shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâ'es shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a cause, then the Persian for a factor, then say \emph{bâ'es shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{باعث} \fa{شدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To cause\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سبب} \fa{شدن} (sabab shodan)}{سبب شدن (sabab shodan)}]{\fa{سبب} \fa{شدن} (sabab shodan) — to bring about, to cause}

\label{lesson:FA-C369-sabab-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a factor, then the Persian for to cause.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سبب} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{سبب} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{sabab shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to bring about, to cause\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{خبر} \fa{سبب} \fa{شد} \fa{که} \fa{همه} \fa{نگران} \fa{شوند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in khabar sabab shod ke hame negarân shavand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This news made everyone worried.
\end{quote}

Like \emph{bâ'es shodan}, a little more formal; \emph{ke} + subjunctive follows.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{سبب}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{sabab} \textquotedblleft{}reason, cause\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is the inherited Persian verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{علت} (be 'ellat-e)}{به علت (be 'ellat-e)}]{\fa{به} \fa{علت} (be 'ellat-e) — owing to, because of}

\label{lesson:FA-C369-be-ellat-e}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to cause, then the Persian for to bring about.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{علت}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{علت}} (\emph{be 'ellat-e}) — \textquotedblleft{}owing to, because of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مدرسه} \fa{به} \fa{علت} \fa{برف} \fa{تعطیل} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{madrese be 'ellat-e barf ta'til shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
School was closed because of the snow.
\end{quote}

Takes a noun with ezafe; for a clause, \emph{be 'ellat-e inke} … . Formal; in speech \emph{be khâter-e}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{علت}} joins the Persian preposition \emph{be} to \emph{'ellat}, from Arabic \emph{'illa} \textquotedblleft{}cause\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): by reason of.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
